title.zh: 卷301 列傳八十八 讷亲 傅恒 福灵安 福隆安 福隆安 丰绅济伦 福长安
title.en: Volume 301 Biographies 88: Ne Qin, Fu Heng, Fu Ling An, Fu Long An, Fu Long An, Feng Shenjilun, Fu Chang An
title.raw: 卷301 列傳八十八 讷亲 傅恒 福灵安 福隆安 福隆安 丰绅济伦 福长安

sentences.zh: 列傳八十八

translations.literal: Biographies 88
translations.idiomatic: Biography 88

sentences.zh: 訥親傅恆子福靈安福隆安福隆安子丰紳濟倫福長安

translations.literal: Neqin, Fu Heng, sons Fu Ling'an, Fu Long'an, Fu Long'an's son Feng Shenjilun, Fu Chang'an
translations.idiomatic: Neqin; Fu Heng; [their sons] Fu Ling'an and Fu Long'an; Fu Long'an's son Feng Shenjilun; Fu Chang'an

sentences.zh: 訥親，鈕祜祿氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，額亦都曾孫。

translations.literal: Neqin, of the Niohuru clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, a great-grandson of Ebilun.
translations.idiomatic: Neqin, of the Niohuru clan, was a Manchu bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner and a great-grandson of Ebilun.

sentences.zh: 父尹德，附見其父遏必隆傳，訥親其次子。

translations.literal: His father Yinde is treated in the biography of his father Ebilun; Neqin was the second son.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yinde is discussed in the biography of Ebilun; Neqin was Yinde's second son.

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，襲公爵，授散秩大臣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng he inherited the dukedom and was appointed minister at large.
translations.idiomatic: In 1727 he inherited the ducal title and was appointed a minister without portfolio.

sentences.zh: 十年，授鑾儀使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed director of the imperial equipage.
translations.idiomatic: In 1732 he was made director of the imperial equipage.

sentences.zh: 十一年十二月，命在辦理軍機處行走。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the eleventh year he was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In late 1733 he was ordered to serve on the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 十三年，世宗疾大漸，訥親預顧命。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the Shizong Emperor fell gravely ill, Neqin was named to the regency council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1735, as the Yongzheng Emperor lay gravely ill, Neqin was named to the regency council.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，莊親王允祿、果親王允禮、鄂爾泰、張廷玉輔政，號「總理王大臣」。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong ascended the throne, Prince Zhuang Yunlu, Prince Guo Yunli, Ortai, and Zhang Tingyu assisted in government under the title 'Chief Ministers in General Affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor took the throne, Prince Zhuang Yunlu, Prince Guo Yunli, Ortai, and Zhang Tingyu formed the regency styled the 'Chief Ministers in General Affairs.'

sentences.zh: 授訥親鑲白旗滿洲都統、領侍衛內大臣，協辦總理事務。

translations.literal: Neqin was appointed Banner General of the Bordered White Banner Manchus and Grand Minister of the Imperial Bodyguard, and assisted in general affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Neqin was made banner general of the Bordered White Banner Manchus and grand minister of the imperial bodyguard, assisting in general affairs.

sentences.zh: 十二月，敕獎訥親勤慎，因推孝昭仁皇后外家恩，進一等公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month an edict praised Neqin's diligence and caution; extending favor to the maternal kin of Empress Xiaozhaoren, he was promoted to duke of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: That December an edict praised Neqin's diligence; in recognition of the empress dowager's kin, he was raised to duke of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年，遷鑲黃旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong he was transferred to Banner General of the Bordered Yellow Banner Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: In 1736 he was transferred to banner general of the Bordered Yellow Banner Manchus.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In 1737 he was appointed minister of war.

sentences.zh: 十一月，莊親王等請罷總理事務，訥親授軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, when the Prince of Zhuang and others requested abolition of the office of general ministerial affairs, Neqin was appointed Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, after the Prince of Zhuang and others asked to abolish the general ministerial board, Neqin was made a grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 敘勞，加拖沙喇哈番世職。

translations.literal: For meritorious service he was granted the hereditary rank of tušan gūsan hafan.
translations.idiomatic: For his services he received the hereditary rank of tušan gūsan hafan.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，領戶部三庫。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year he took charge of the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In February 1738 he assumed charge of the three treasuries of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 九月，命協辦戶部。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was ordered to assist in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In September he was ordered to assist at the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 直隸總督李衛劾總河硃藻詐欺貪虐，命訥親與尚書孫嘉淦勘讞，藻坐流。

translations.literal: Zhili Governor Li Wei impeached Director-General of Rivers Zhu Zao for fraud, oppression, and corruption; Neqin was ordered with Minister Sun Jia'en to investigate and try the case; Zhu was sentenced to banishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhili governor Li Wei accused river director Zhu Zao of fraud and corruption, Neqin and Minister Sun Jia'en were sent to investigate; Zhu was sentenced to exile.

sentences.zh: 訥親因與嘉淦條上永定河南北岸建築閘壩諸事。

translations.literal: Neqin, together with Jia'en, memorialized item by item on building sluices and dams along the north and south banks of the Yongding River.
translations.idiomatic: Neqin and Jia'en also submitted a detailed memorial on sluices and dams along both banks of the Yongding River.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In December he was transferred to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was given the honorary title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In May 1739 he received the honorary title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 訥親貴戚勳舊，少侍禁近，受世宗知，以為可大用。

translations.literal: Neqin was a noble by birth and a meritorious minister; from youth he attended close to the throne and won the Shizong Emperor's trust, who regarded him as fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: A noble by birth and a minister of long standing merit, Neqin had served near the throne from youth and won Yongzheng's trust as a man fit for high office.

sentences.zh: 迨高宗，恩眷尤厚。

translations.literal: Under the Gaozong, favor and grace were especially thick.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong his favor was especially deep.

sentences.zh: 訥親勤敏當上意，尤以廉介自敕，人不敢干以私。

translations.literal: Neqin was diligent and alert in suiting the emperor's wishes, and above all restrained himself with integrity; no one dared approach him for private favors.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent and attentive to the emperor's wishes, he above all held himself to strict integrity, and no one dared solicit him privately.

sentences.zh: 其居第巨獒縛扉側，絕無車馬跡。

translations.literal: At his residence a huge mastiff was tied beside the gate; there was never a trace of carriage or horse traffic.
translations.idiomatic: At his house a huge mastiff was tied beside the gate, and no carriage or horse ever came to call.

sentences.zh: 然以早貴，意氣驕溢，治事務刻深。

translations.literal: Yet having risen to high rank early, his spirit was proud and overbearing, and in handling affairs he was invariably harsh and severe.
translations.idiomatic: Yet having risen early to high rank, he grew proud and overbearing, and in office he was relentlessly harsh.

sentences.zh: 左都御史劉統勳疏論訥親領事過多，任事過銳。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Liu Tongxun memorialized criticizing Neqin for holding too many posts and for being too sharp in discharge of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Liu Tongxun memorialized that Neqin held too many posts and was too sharp in his handling of affairs.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「訥親為尚書，模棱推諉，固所不可，但治事未當，亦所不免，朕時時戒毋自滿。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed: 'Neqin as Minister—evasive shirking is certainly not permissible, but it is also unavoidable that his handling of affairs is sometimes not right; I constantly warn him not to be self-satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: 'As minister, Neqin must not be evasive or shirking—but it is also inevitable that he sometimes mishandles affairs; I constantly warn him against self-satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 今見此奏，益當自勉。」

translations.literal: Now that I see this memorial, he should strive all the more to improve.'
translations.idiomatic: Now that I see this memorial, he should strive all the more to improve.'

sentences.zh: 語詳統勳傳。

translations.literal: The full account is in Liu Tongxun's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full exchange is recorded in Liu Tongxun's biography.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，命訥親閱河南、江南、山東諸省營伍，並勘海塘、河工。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year Neqin was ordered to inspect military colonies in Henan, Jiangnan, and Shandong, and also to survey the sea wall and river works.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1744 Neqin was ordered to inspect troops in Henan, Jiangnan, and Shandong and to survey sea walls and river works.

sentences.zh: 時直隸天津、河間二府方以災治賑，令順道先往察覈。

translations.literal: At that time the Tianjin and Hejian prefectures of Zhili were providing famine relief; he was ordered to go first by the way to inspect and verify.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin and Hejian in Zhili were then under famine relief, and he was told to go first by the way to inspect.

sentences.zh: 疏請展賑一月，從之。

translations.literal: He memorialized to extend relief by one month; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to extend relief by one month, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 訥親使事既蕆，分疏上陳，其勘諸省營伍，言：「遍閱三省督撫、河漕、提鎮為標者十七，優絀互見。

translations.literal: When Neqin's mission was concluded, he submitted separate memorials; on inspecting the military colonies of the several provinces he said: 'Having read through the standards of the governors-general, governors, grain transport commissioners, and provincial commanders of the three provinces, merits and demerits were mixed.
translations.idiomatic: When his tour was finished, Neqin submitted separate memorials; on the troops of the three provinces he wrote: 'Having reviewed the standards set by the governors-general, governors, grain commissioners, and regional commanders—seventeen in all—merit and demerit were mixed.

sentences.zh: 惟河南南陽、江南蘇松水師二鎮最劣。

translations.literal: Only the Nanyang garrison in Henan and the Suzhou-Songjiang naval garrison in Jiangnan were the worst.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Nanyang garrison in Henan and the Suzhou-Songjiang naval command in Jiangnan ranked worst.

sentences.zh: 請下部覈賞罰。」

translations.literal: Request that the ministry verify rewards and punishments.'
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the ministries verify rewards and punishments.'

sentences.zh: 其勘江、浙海塘，言：「舊日浙江潮自蜀山中小亹出入，近海寧為北大亹，近蕭山為南大亹，漲沙寬闊，為杭州、紹興二府保障。

translations.literal: On inspecting the sea walls of Jiangsu and Zhejiang he said: 'Formerly the Zhejiang tide entered and left by the Small Waist at Shushan; near Haining was the Great Northern Waist and near Xiaoshan the Great Southern Waist; the broad accretion of silt served as a safeguard for Hangzhou and Shaoxing prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On the Jiangsu and Zhejiang sea walls he wrote: 'Formerly the Zhejiang tide passed through the Small Waist at Shushan; near Haining lay the Great Northern Waist and near Xiaoshan the Great Southern Waist, and the broad buildup of sand protected Hangzhou and Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 迨中小亹漸湮，潮趨蜀山北，震盪為患。

translations.literal: After the Small Waist gradually silted up, the tide turned north of Shushan and in its surge became a calamity.
translations.idiomatic: After the Small Waist gradually silted shut, the tide shifted north of Shushan and surged destructively.

sentences.zh: 若濬中小亹故道，減大亹潮力，上下塘工悉可安堵；

translations.literal: If the old course of the Small Waist were dredged to reduce the force of the Great Waists, the upper and lower embankment works could all be secured;
translations.idiomatic: If the old channel of the Small Waist were dredged to weaken the Great Waists, upper and lower embankments could all be secured;

sentences.zh: 即中小亹未可遽复，則當擇險要多為坦坡，木石戧壩，俾撇水積淤資以御潮。

translations.literal: even if the Small Waist could not soon be restored, then dangerous points should be chosen and ramparts of earth, timber, and stone wing-dams built so that diverted water might deposit silt to help resist the tide.
translations.idiomatic: even if the Small Waist could not soon be restored, dangerous points should be faced with earthen slopes and timber-and-stone wing-dams so diverted water might deposit silt against the tide.

sentences.zh: 至諸處柴塘，停沙阻水，無煩議改石工。

translations.literal: As for the wattled embankments everywhere, they detain sand and obstruct water—there is no need to discuss converting them to stone works.
translations.idiomatic: As for wattled embankments elsewhere, they hold sand and obstruct water—there is no need to convert them to stone.

sentences.zh: 入江南境，地平而潮緩，華亭舊塘堅緻，寶山新塘尺度參差，工作又不中程。

translations.literal: Entering Jiangnan territory, where the land is level and the tide slack, the old embankment at Huating was solid and tight; the new embankment at Baoshan varied in dimensions and the work also fell short of specification.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangnan, where the land is flat and the tide slow, Huating's old dike was solid, but Baoshan's new dike varied in size and the workmanship fell short.

sentences.zh: 金山、奉賢、南匯、上海皆土塘，距海稍遠，所司守護如法，當無他虞。」

translations.literal: Jinshan, Fengxian, Nanhui, and Shanghai are all earthen dikes, somewhat distant from the sea; if those in charge maintain them according to rule, there should be no other worry.'
translations.idiomatic: Jinshan, Fengxian, Nanhui, and Shanghai all have earthen dikes somewhat inland; if maintained properly, they should give no further trouble.'

sentences.zh: 其勘洪澤湖，請濬鹽河俾通江，疏串場河俾達海，並停天然二壩、高堰下游二堤。

translations.literal: On surveying Hongze Lake, he requested dredging the Salt River to connect with the Yangtze, clearing the Chuan-chang Canal to reach the sea, and halting the two dams at Tianran and the two dikes below Gaoyan.
translations.idiomatic: On Hongze Lake he asked to dredge the Salt River to the Yangtze, clear the Chuan-chang Canal to the sea, and halt the two Tianran dams and the two dikes below Gaoyan.

sentences.zh: 其勘南旺湖，請以湖中涸地貸貧民耕稼。

translations.literal: On surveying Nanwang Lake, he requested leasing dried land in the lake to poor peasants for cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: On Nanwang Lake he proposed leasing dried lake bed to poor peasants for farming.

sentences.zh: 別疏言：「各直省政事，督撫下司道，司道下州縣，州縣官惟以簿書錢穀為事，戶口貧富、土地肥瘠、物產豐嗇、民情向背、風俗美惡、以及山川原隰、橋樑道路，皆漫置不省。

translations.literal: In a separate memorial he said: 'In each province, local government descends from governor-general and governor to circuit intendant, and from intendant to prefecture and county; county magistrates concern themselves only with ledgers, cash, and grain. Household wealth and poverty, soil fertility, abundance of products, popular inclinations, customs good or bad, mountains and plains, bridges and roads—all are casually disregarded.
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he said: 'In every province administration runs from governor-general and governor to circuit intendant and then to prefecture and county; magistrates busy themselves only with ledgers, cash, and grain. Household wealth and poverty, soil quality, local products, popular sentiment, customs, terrain, bridges, and roads—all are ignored.

sentences.zh: 官但有條教，民惟責納賦，浮文常多，實意殊少。

translations.literal: Officials have only statutes and orders; the people are held only to paying tax; empty documents are many, real intent very little.
translations.idiomatic: Officials issue regulations; the people owe only taxes; paperwork abounds while real concern is slight.

sentences.zh: 請敕各直省督撫，令州縣官遍歷境內，何事當興舉，何事當整飭，行之有無治效，以實報長官，長官即是為殿最，以實達朝廷。

translations.literal: Request an edict to each governor-general and governor to order county magistrates to traverse their jurisdictions, what should be promoted, what rectified, whether execution has yielded results—all reported truthfully to superiors; superiors take this as the basis of evaluation, reported truthfully to court.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that governors-general and governors order magistrates to tour their districts, report what should be promoted or rectified and with what effect, so superiors could grade them honestly for the court.

sentences.zh: 似亦崇實效、去虛文、飭吏治、厚民生之一端也。」

translations.literal: This seems also one means of honoring real effect, removing empty documents, rectifying officialdom, and enriching people's livelihood.'
translations.idiomatic: This would be one way to prize results over empty forms, tighten administration, and benefit the people.'

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: All were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: All proposals were sent to the ministries for deliberation and action.

sentences.zh: 十年三月，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year he was appointed associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1745 he was appointed associate grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 五月，授保和殿大學士，仍兼吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony, while still holding the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he became grand secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony while retaining the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十二年四月，命如山西會巡撫愛必達讞萬全民張世祿、安邑民張遠等挾眾抗官狀，論如律。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twelfth year he was ordered to Shanxi to join Governor Ai Bida in trying the case of Zhang Shilu of Wanmin and Zhang Yuan of Anyi and others who led crowds in resisting officials; judgment was according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of 1747 he was sent to Shanxi to join Governor Ai Bida in trying Zhang Shilu of Wanmin, Zhang Yuan of Anyi, and others who had led mobs against officials; all were sentenced by law.

sentences.zh: 愛必達及總兵羅俊、蒲州知府硃發等皆坐譴黜。

translations.literal: Ai Bida, Commander-in-chief Luo Jun, Pu prefect Zhu Fa, and others were all reprimanded and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Ai Bida, Commander Luo Jun, Pu prefect Zhu Fa, and others were all reprimanded and removed.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，命如浙江會大學士高斌覆勘巡撫常安貪婪狀，未至，高斌鞫得常安實受賕，訥親與共奏，論如律。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year he was ordered to Zhejiang to join Grand Secretary Gao Bin in re-investigating Governor Chang An's corruption; before his arrival Gao Bin had already obtained proof that Chang An had indeed taken bribes; Neqin joined in the memorial; judgment was according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1748 he was ordered to Zhejiang to join Grand Secretary Gao Bin in reinvestigating Governor Chang An; before he arrived, Gao Bin had proved Chang An's bribes, and Neqin joined the memorial; sentence followed the law.

sentences.zh: 三月，復命如山東會巡撫阿里袞治賑。

translations.literal: In the third month he was again ordered to Shandong to join Governor Aligun in famine relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was again sent to Shandong to join Governor Aligun in famine relief.

sentences.zh: 時大金川土司莎羅奔攻革布什咱土司犯邊，上命川陝總督張廣泗討之。

translations.literal: At that time the Jinchuan chieftain Slob Dpon attacked the Gbashi-za tribal chief and violated the border; the emperor ordered Sichuan-Shaanxi Governor-General Zhang Guangsi to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinchuan chieftain Slob Dpon had attacked the Gbashi-za chief and raided the border; the emperor ordered Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general Zhang Guangsi to punish him.

sentences.zh: 大金川地絕險，阻山為石壘，名曰碉，師進攻弗克。

translations.literal: Jinchuan terrain was utterly precipitous; blocking mountains they built stone fortresses called diao; the army attacked but could not take them.
translations.idiomatic: Jinchuan country was utterly rugged; the people blocked the mountains with stone fortresses called diao, and the army could not break them.

sentences.zh: 四月，召訥親還京師，授經略大臣，率禁旅出視師。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Neqin was recalled to the capital and appointed commander-in-chief, leading the Gendarmerie to oversee the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Neqin was recalled to the capital, made commander-in-chief, and sent at the head of the Gendarmerie to oversee the campaign.

sentences.zh: 六月，訥親至軍，下令期三日克噶拉依，噶拉依者，莎羅奔結寨地也。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Neqin reached the army and ordered that within three days Gala-i should be taken—Gala-i being Slob Dpon's fortified place.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Neqin reached the front and ordered Gala-i—Slob Dpon's stronghold—taken within three days.

sentences.zh: 師循色爾力石梁而下，攻碉未即克，署總兵任舉勇敢善戰，為諸軍先，沒於陣。

translations.literal: The army advanced down the Serli Stone Beam to attack the diao but did not immediately take them; Acting Brigadier Ren Ju, brave and skilled in battle, led all armies in the van and fell in action.
translations.idiomatic: The army marched down the Serli Stone Beam to assault the diao without immediate success; acting brigadier Ren Ju, brave in battle, led the van and fell.

sentences.zh: 訥親為氣奪，乃議督諸軍築碉，與敵共險，為持久。

translations.literal: Neqin lost his nerve and then proposed urging all armies to build diao, sharing the peril with the enemy, for a prolonged campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Neqin lost heart and proposed that all forces build diao of their own, sharing the terrain with the enemy for a war of attrition.

sentences.zh: 疏入，上重失任舉，又以築碉非計，手詔戒訥親，因時度勢，以為進止。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor deeply regretted the loss of Ren Ju and also held that building diao was no plan; he personally drafted an edict warning Neqin to gauge time and circumstance in deciding advance or retreat.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor mourned Ren Ju deeply and held that building diao was folly; he personally drafted an edict telling Neqin to weigh time and circumstance in advancing or holding back.

sentences.zh: 訥親與廣泗合疏言：「天時地利皆賊得其長，我兵無機可乘。

translations.literal: Neqin and Guangsi jointly memorialized: 'Heaven's season and earth's terrain the enemy hold to their advantage; our troops have no opening to exploit.
translations.idiomatic: Neqin and Guangsi jointly wrote: 'Season and terrain favor the enemy; our troops find no opening.

sentences.zh: 冬春間當減兵駐守，明歲加調精銳三萬，於四月進剿，足以成功，至遲亦不逾秋令。」

translations.literal: Between winter and spring troops should be reduced for garrison; next year thirty thousand picked troops should be added to advance in the fourth month—enough to succeed, at the latest not beyond autumn.'
translations.idiomatic: Between winter and spring we should reduce the army to garrison duty; next year add thirty thousand picked men and advance in the fourth month—success is assured, or at latest by autumn.'

sentences.zh: 訥親又別疏言：「來歲增兵，計需費數百萬。

translations.literal: Neqin also separately memorialized: 'Adding troops next year will require several million in expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Neqin also wrote separately: 'Reinforcements next year will cost several million.

sentences.zh: 若俟二三年後有機可乘，亦未可定。」

translations.literal: If one waits two or three years until an opening appears—that too cannot be fixed.'
translations.idiomatic: If we wait two or three years for an opening, that too cannot be foretold.'

sentences.zh: 疏入，上諭曰：「卿等身在戎行，目擊情狀，不能確有成算，游移兩可。

translations.literal: When the memorials arrived, the emperor instructed: 'You are in the field and see the situation with your own eyes yet cannot settle on a sure plan, wavering between two options.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorials arrived, the emperor said: 'You are in the field and see the situation yet cannot fix a plan, wavering between two courses.

sentences.zh: 朕於數千里外，何從遙度？

translations.literal: I am thousands of li away—how can I judge from afar?
translations.idiomatic: I am thousands of li away—how can I judge from afar?

sentences.zh: 我師至四萬，彼止三千餘，何以彼應我則有餘，我攻彼則不足？

translations.literal: Our army reaches forty thousand; they have only three thousand-odd—why do they have enough to answer us yet we have not enough to attack them?
translations.idiomatic: Our force is forty thousand; they have barely three thousand—why do they have enough to meet us while we lack enough to attack?

sentences.zh: 卿等當審定應攻應罷，毋為兩歧語。」

translations.literal: You must decide whether to attack or withdraw; do not use ambiguous language.'
translations.idiomatic: Decide whether to attack or withdraw; do not speak with a forked tongue.'

sentences.zh: 上知訥親不足辦敵，諭軍機大臣議召訥親還；

translations.literal: The emperor knew Neqin was unequal to the enemy and instructed the Grand Councillors to deliberate recalling Neqin;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew Neqin could not handle the enemy and told the grand councillors to consider recalling him;

sentences.zh: 又念大金川非大敵，重臣視師，無功而還，傷國體，為四夷姍笑。

translations.literal: yet he also reflected that Jinchuan was no great foe and that a high minister overseeing the army returning without success would injure national dignity and invite the ridicule of the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: yet he also thought that Jinchuan was no great enemy, and that a senior minister returning without victory would wound the state's dignity and invite ridicule from the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 密以諭訥親，冀激奮克敵。

translations.literal: He secretly so informed Neqin, hoping to stir him to exertion in defeating the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly told Neqin as much, hoping to stir him to defeat the enemy.

sentences.zh: 居數月，師雖有小胜，卒未得尺寸地。

translations.literal: After several months, though the army had small victories, in the end not a foot of ground was gained.
translations.idiomatic: After several months the army won small fights but gained not a foot of ground.

sentences.zh: 訥親惟請還京面對，乃召訥親及廣泗詣京師，以岳鍾琪攝經略，傅爾丹攝川陝總督，復遣尚書班第同治軍事。

translations.literal: Neqin only asked to return to the capital for audience face to face; then Neqin and Guangsi were summoned to the capital; Yue Zhongqi was appointed acting commander-in-chief, Fu Erdan acting Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general; Minister Ban Di was again sent to jointly manage military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Neqin could only ask to return to the capital for audience; Neqin and Guangsi were summoned; Yue Zhongqi became acting commander-in-chief, Fu Erdan acting Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general, and Minister Ban Di was again sent to manage affairs jointly.

sentences.zh: 尋奪訥親官，令自具鞍馬，從討噶爾丹贖罪，逮廣泗。

translations.literal: Soon Neqin's office was stripped and he was ordered to provide his own saddle and horse and follow the campaign against the Eleuths to redeem his crime; Guangsi was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Neqin was stripped of rank and ordered to furnish his own horse and follow the campaign against the Eleuths to redeem his guilt; Guangsi was arrested.

sentences.zh: 九月，命大學士傅恆代為經略，別遣侍衛富成逮訥親，責置對，並令富成錄訥親舉止言語以聞。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the emperor ordered Grand Secretary Fu Heng to replace him as commander-in-chief; a separate envoy, guard Fu Cheng, was sent to arrest Neqin, take him for questioning, and record Neqin's conduct and speech to report.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Grand Secretary Fu Heng was made commander-in-chief in his place; guard Fu Cheng was sent separately to arrest Neqin, question him, and report his words and conduct.

sentences.zh: 上前後手詔罪訥親恆數千百言，略謂：「訥親受命總戎，乖張畏縮。

translations.literal: The emperor's successive personal edicts condemning Neqin ran to thousands of words, in summary: 'Neqin received command as commander-in-chief yet was perverse, fearful, and shrinking.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's successive personal edicts condemning Neqin ran to thousands of words, saying in sum: 'Neqin took command as commander-in-chief yet was perverse, fearful, and shrinking.

sentences.zh: 疏言軍夜攻碉，自帳中望見火光，知未嘗臨敵。

translations.literal: He reported that in night attacks on diao he watched the firelight from his tent and knew he had never faced the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote that during night attacks on diao he watched the fire from his tent and had never faced the enemy.

sentences.zh: 又言督軍攻阿利山，既回營，我軍數十人各鳥獸散。

translations.literal: He also said supervising the army at attack on Ali Mountain—having returned to camp, our several score men scattered each like birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: He also said that supervising the assault on Ali Mountain, he returned to camp while several dozen of our men scattered like birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 知偶臨敵，又先士卒退。

translations.literal: Knowing he faced the enemy only by chance, he again retreated before his men.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he faced the enemy only by chance, he again fell back ahead of his men.

sentences.zh: 富成疏訥親語'金川事大難，不可輕舉，此言不敢入奏'。

translations.literal: Fu Cheng reported Neqin's words: 'The Jinchuan affair is very difficult and cannot be lightly undertaken—this I dare not enter in a memorial.'
translations.idiomatic: Fu Cheng reported Neqin's words: 'The Jinchuan affair is very hard and cannot be lightly undertaken—I dare not put this in a memorial.'

sentences.zh: 訥親受恩久，何事不可言？

translations.literal: Neqin received grace so long—what could he not speak?
translations.idiomatic: Neqin had received favor so long—what could he not say?

sentences.zh: 如固不能克，當實陳請罷兵。

translations.literal: If he truly could not conquer, he ought honestly to have memorialized requesting withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: If he truly could not win, he should have honestly memorialized to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 乃事敗欲以不可輕舉歸過朝廷，狡詐出意外。

translations.literal: When affairs failed he wished to lay the blame on the court for 'not lightly undertaking'—cunning beyond expectation.
translations.idiomatic: When affairs failed he wished to blame the court for 'not lightly undertaking'—cunning beyond expectation.

sentences.zh: 又值續調兵過，輒言'此皆我罪，令如許滿洲兵受苦'。

translations.literal: Again when reinforcements continued to arrive he would say 'This is all my fault, making so many Manchu soldiers suffer.'
translations.idiomatic: Again when reinforcements arrived he would say, 'This is all my fault, making so many Manchu soldiers suffer.'

sentences.zh: 滿洲兵聞調，鼓舞振躍，志切同仇。

translations.literal: Manchu soldiers hearing of transfer leaped and rejoiced, eager to avenge together.
translations.idiomatic: Manchu soldiers hearing of transfer leaped for joy, eager to fight as one.

sentences.zh: 訥親以為受苦，實嫉他人成功，搖眾心，不顧國事。

translations.literal: Neqin took this for suffering—in truth he envied others' success, shook the troops' hearts, and disregarded state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Neqin called this suffering—in truth he envied others' success, shook the army's heart, and disregarded the state's business.

sentences.zh: 孤恩藐法，罪不可逭。」

translations.literal: Ungrateful, contemptuous of law—crime cannot be excused.'
translations.idiomatic: Ungrateful and contemptuous of law—his crime could not be pardoned.'

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark of the imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: End of the imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 十月，諭「訥親先世以軍功封二等公，為孝昭仁皇后戚屬，供職勤慎，進一等公。

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict stated: 'Neqin's forebears were enfeoffed duke of the second rank for military merit; as consort kin of Empress Xiaozhaoren he served diligently and was advanced to duke of the first rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month an edict said: 'Neqin's forebears were enfeoffed duke of the second rank for military merit; as kin of Empress Xiaozhaoren he served diligently and was raised to duke of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 獲罪，應仍以二等公俾其兄策楞襲爵」。

translations.literal: Having incurred guilt, he should still revert to duke of the second rank for his elder brother Celeng to inherit.'
translations.idiomatic: Having incurred guilt, the title should still revert to duke of the second rank for his elder brother Celeng to inherit.'

sentences.zh: 訥親恃上恩，尚冀入見上自解，上复迭降手詔，謂：「軍旅事重，平日治事詳慎，操守潔清，舉不足言。」

translations.literal: Neqin relied on imperial favor and still hoped on audience to explain himself; the emperor again repeatedly issued personal edicts saying: 'Military affairs weigh heavily; usual diligence in office and clean integrity are not worth mentioning.'
translations.idiomatic: Neqin relied on imperial favor and still hoped to explain himself at audience; the emperor again sent personal edicts: 'Military affairs weigh heavily; ordinary diligence and clean integrity count for nothing.'

sentences.zh: 又謂：「訥親小心謹密，而方寸一壞，天奪其魄，雖欲倖免而不能。」

translations.literal: Also he said: 'Neqin was cautious and close in small things, but once his mind turned corrupt heaven took his wits—even wishing to escape he could not.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also said: 'Neqin was cautious in small things, but once his mind turned corrupt heaven took his wits—even wishing to escape, he could not.'

sentences.zh: 十二月，廣泗既誅，上封遏必隆遺刀授侍衛鄂實，監訥親還軍，誅以警眾。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Guangsi having been executed, the emperor sealed Ebilun's heirloom sword and gave it to guard E Shi to escort Neqin back to the army and execute him to warn the host.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, after Guangsi was executed, the emperor sealed Ebilun's heirloom sword and gave it to guard E Shi to escort Neqin back to the army and execute him as a warning.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，上命傅恆班師，复諭鄂實即途中行法。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year the emperor ordered Fu Heng to withdraw the army and again instructed E Shi to carry out the sentence on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1749 the emperor ordered Fu Heng to withdraw the army and told E Shi to carry out the sentence on the road.

sentences.zh: 是月戊寅，鄂實監訥親行至班攔山，聞後命，遂誅訥親。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin of that month, E Shi escorting Neqin reached Banlan Mountain; hearing the later order, he then executed Neqin.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day of that month, E Shi escorting Neqin reached Banlan Mountain; hearing the later order, he executed Neqin.

sentences.zh: 傅恆，字春和，富察氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人，孝賢純皇后弟也。

translations.literal: Fu Heng, style Chunhe, of the Fuca clan, Manchu Bordered Yellow Banner, was younger brother of Empress Xiaoxianchun.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng, whose style was Chunhe, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner and younger brother of Empress Xiaoxianchun.

sentences.zh: 父李榮保，附見其父米思翰傳。

translations.literal: His father Li Rongbao is treated in the biography of his father Misanhan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Rongbao is discussed in the biography of Misanhan.

sentences.zh: 傅恆自侍衛洊擢戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Fu Heng was promoted step by step from guard to vice-minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng rose from the guards to vice-minister of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十年六月，命在軍機處行走。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the tenth year of Qianlong he was ordered to serve in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In June 1745 he was ordered to serve on the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1747 he was made minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 十三年三月，孝賢純皇后從上南巡，還至德州崩，傅恆扈行，典喪儀。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year, when Empress Xiaoxianchun accompanied the emperor on a southern tour and died at Dezhou on the return, Fu Heng attended the journey and directed the mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: In March 1748 Empress Xiaoxianchun died at Dezhou on the southern tour; Fu Heng had accompanied the emperor and directed the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 四月，敕獎其勤恪，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fourth month an edict praised his diligence and granted him the honorary title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In April an edict praised his diligence and made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 時訥親視師金川，解尚書阿克敦協辦大學士以授傅恆，並兼領吏部。

translations.literal: At that time Neqin was commanding the army in Jinchuan; Minister Aikedun was relieved as associate grand secretary and the post given to Fu Heng, who also concurrently headed the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: While Neqin commanded in Jinchuan, Minister Aikedun was replaced as associate grand secretary by Fu Heng, who also took charge of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 訥親既無功，九月，命傅恆暫管川陝總督，經略軍務。

translations.literal: After Neqin's failure, in the ninth month Fu Heng was ordered temporarily to administer the Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-generalship and command military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Neqin's failure, in the ninth month Fu Heng was ordered to act as Sichuan-Shaanxi governor-general and take command of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 尋授保和殿大學士，發京師及諸行省滿、漢兵三萬五千，以部庫及諸行省銀四百萬供軍儲，又出內帑十萬備犒賞。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony; thirty-five thousand Manchu and Han troops from the capital and provinces were sent out, four million taels from the ministries and provinces supplied the army, and one hundred thousand taels from the privy purse were issued for rewards.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand secretary of the Hall of Preserving Harmony; 35,000 Manchu and Han troops marched out with four million taels for supplies and 100,000 taels from the privy purse for rewards.

sentences.zh: 十一月，師行，上詣堂子告察，遣皇子及大學士來保等送至良鄉。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the army set out; the emperor went to the Tangzi to offer sacrifice and sent princes and Grand Secretary Lai Bao and others to see Fu Heng off to Liangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In November the army marched; the emperor sacrificed at the Tangzi and sent princes and Grand Secretary Lai Bao to escort Fu Heng to Liangxiang.

sentences.zh: 傅恆既行，上日降手詔褒勉。

translations.literal: After Fu Heng departed, the emperor daily sent personal edicts of praise and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Heng left, the emperor sent him personal edicts of praise each day.

sentences.zh: 傅恆道陝西，言驛政不修誤軍興，上命協辦大學士尚書尹繼善攝陝西總督，主饋運。

translations.literal: Fu Heng, passing through Shaanxi, reported that neglected courier service was delaying the army; the emperor ordered Associate Grand Secretary and Minister Yin Jishan to act as Shaanxi governor-general and manage transport.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Shaanxi, Fu Heng reported that bad courier service was hindering the army; Yin Jishan was ordered to act as Shaanxi governor-general and handle supply.

sentences.zh: 入四川境，馬不給，上又命尹繼善往來川、陝督察。

translations.literal: Entering Sichuan, horses were lacking; the emperor again ordered Yin Jishan to travel between Sichuan and Shaanxi to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan horses were scarce; Yin Jishan was again ordered to supervise between Sichuan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 旋以傅恆師行甚速，紀律嚴明，命議敘，部議加太子太傅，特命加太保。

translations.literal: Soon, because Fu Heng's march was very rapid and discipline strict, he was recommended for reward; the ministry proposed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, but the emperor specially ordered Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Heng's march proved swift and discipline strict, the ministry proposed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent; the emperor instead made him Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 固辭，不允，發京師及山西、湖北馬七千佐軍。

translations.literal: He firmly declined but was not allowed; seven thousand horses from the capital and Shanxi and Hubei were sent to support the army.
translations.idiomatic: He declined firmly but was overruled; 7,000 horses from the capital, Shanxi, and Hubei were sent to the army.

sentences.zh: 傅恆發成都，經天赦山，雪後道險，步行七十里至驛。

translations.literal: Fu Heng set out from Chengdu, passed Tianshe Mountain; after snow the road was perilous and he walked seventy li to the post station.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Chengdu he crossed Tianshe Mountain; after snow the road was treacherous and he walked seventy li to the next station.

sentences.zh: 上聞，賜雙眼孔雀翎，复固辭。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he bestowed a double-eyed peacock feather; Fu Heng again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this the emperor gave him a double-eyed peacock feather, which Fu Heng again declined.

sentences.zh: 初，小金川土舍良爾吉間其兄澤旺於莎羅奔，奪其印，即烝於嫂阿扣。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Liang Erji had turned his brother Zewang over to Slob Dpon, seized his seal, and took his sister-in-law A Kou in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lesser Jinchuan chieftain Liang Erji had betrayed his brother Zewang to Slob Dpon, seized his seal, and taken his sister-in-law A Kou.

sentences.zh: 莎羅奔之犯邊也，良爾吉實從之，後詐降為賊諜。

translations.literal: When Slob Dpon raided the border, Liang Erji had in fact followed him; later he feigned surrender and served as the enemy's spy.
translations.idiomatic: When Slob Dpon invaded, Liang Erji had aided him; later he pretended to surrender and spied for the enemy.

sentences.zh: 張廣泗入奸民王秋言，使領蠻兵，我師舉動，賊輒知之。

translations.literal: Zhang Guangsi trusted the traitor Wang Qiu, who led barbarian troops; our army's every move the enemy learned at once.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangsi trusted the traitor Wang Qiu, who led tribal troops, so the enemy always knew our movements.

sentences.zh: 傅恆途中疏請誅良爾吉等，將至軍，使副將馬良柱招良爾吉來迎，至邦噶山，正其罪，並阿扣、王秋悉誅之。

translations.literal: Fu Heng memorialized on the road requesting execution of Liang Erji and others; nearing the army he had Deputy Commander Ma Liangzhu summon Liang Erji to welcome him; at Bangga Mountain he tried their crimes and executed Liang Erji, A Kou, and Wang Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: En route Fu Heng asked to execute Liang Erji; near the front he had Ma Liangzhu summon Liang Erji to Bangga Mountain, tried him, and executed him with A Kou and Wang Qiu.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上褒傅恆明斷，命拜前賜雙眼孔雀翎，毋更固辭。

translations.literal: When the report arrived, the emperor praised Fu Heng's decisiveness and ordered him to accept the earlier gift of the double-eyed peacock feather without further refusal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Fu Heng's decisiveness and told him to accept the peacock feather he had earlier refused.

sentences.zh: 十月，至卡撒，以屯軍地狹隘，與賊相望，且雜處番民巿肆中，乃相度移舊壘前，令總兵冶大雄監營壘。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he reached Kasa; finding the garrison ground narrow and facing the enemy amid tribal markets, he chose a site before the old camp and had Commander Ye Daxiong supervise building the encampment.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he reached Kasa; the camp was cramped and mixed with tribal markets, so he moved the lines forward under Ye Daxiong's supervision.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，上疏言：「臣至軍，察用兵始末：當紀山進討之始，馬良柱轉戰而前，逾沃日收小金川直抵丹噶，其鋒甚銳。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year he memorialized: 'Having reached the army, I examined the whole course of the campaign: when Ji Shan first advanced, Ma Liangzhu fought forward, crossed Wo Ri, took Lesser Jinchuan, and reached Danga—his momentum was very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1749 he wrote: 'At the army I reviewed the campaign: when Ji Shan first attacked, Ma Liangzhu fought through Wo Ri, took Lesser Jinchuan, and reached Danga with great momentum.

sentences.zh: 彼時張廣泗若速進師，賊備未嚴，殄滅尚易；

translations.literal: If Zhang Guangsi had then pressed forward quickly, the enemy's defenses were not yet firm and extermination would still have been easy;
translations.idiomatic: Had Zhang Guangsi advanced quickly then, the enemy was unprepared and could have been destroyed easily;

sentences.zh: 乃坐失事機，宋宗璋宿留於雜穀，許應虎敗衄於的郊，賊得盡據險要，增碉備禦。

translations.literal: but he lost the moment; Song Zongzhang lingered at Zagu, Xu Yinghu was defeated at Dijiao, and the enemy held all the passes and strengthened their diao defenses.
translations.idiomatic: instead he lost the moment; Song Zongzhang stalled at Zagu, Xu Yinghu was beaten at Dijiao, and the enemy held the passes and strengthened their diao.

sentences.zh: 訥親初至，督戰甚急，任舉敗沒，銳挫氣索，軍無鬥志，一以軍事委張廣泗。

translations.literal: When Neqin first arrived he urged battle fiercely; Ren Ju was defeated and killed, spirits were broken and the army lost will to fight, and he left all military affairs to Zhang Guangsi.
translations.idiomatic: When Neqin arrived he pressed battle hard; Ren Ju fell, morale collapsed, and he handed everything to Zhang Guangsi.

sentences.zh: 廣泗又為奸人所愚，專主攻碉。

translations.literal: Guangsi was again deceived by traitors and devoted himself solely to assaulting diao.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi was fooled by traitors and attacked only diao.

sentences.zh: 先後殺傷數千人，匿不以聞。

translations.literal: Thousands were killed or wounded before and after, and he concealed it without reporting.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands were killed or wounded, which he hid from reports.

sentences.zh: 臣惟攻碉最為下策，槍砲不能洞堅壁，於賊無所傷。

translations.literal: I hold that assaulting diao is the worst stratagem; muskets and cannon cannot pierce solid walls and do the enemy no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Assaulting diao is the worst plan: guns cannot breach solid walls or harm the enemy.

sentences.zh: 賊不過數人，自暗擊明，槍不虛發。

translations.literal: The enemy are but a few men; shooting from darkness at those in the light, not a shot is wasted.
translations.idiomatic: A few men in the dark shoot at many in the light, and every shot tells.

sentences.zh: 是我惟攻石，而賊實攻人。

translations.literal: Thus we attack only stone while the enemy in fact attack men.
translations.idiomatic: We strike stone while the enemy strike men.

sentences.zh: 賊於碉外為濠，兵不能越，賊伏其中，自下擊上。

translations.literal: Outside the diao the enemy dig moats our troops cannot cross; hidden within, they strike from below upward.
translations.idiomatic: They dig moats we cannot cross and fire downward from within.

sentences.zh: 其碉銳立，高於浮屠，建作甚捷，數日可成，旋缺旋補。

translations.literal: The diao stand sharp, higher than pagodas; they are built very quickly, finished in days, repaired as fast as they fall.
translations.idiomatic: The diao rise like pagodas, built in days and patched as fast as they crumble.

sentences.zh: 且眾心甚固，碉盡碎而不去，砲方過而復起。

translations.literal: The people's hearts are very firm; though diao are shattered they do not leave, and when cannon pass they rise again.
translations.idiomatic: The people stand firm: when diao are smashed they do not flee, and when cannon pass they rebuild.

sentences.zh: 客主勞佚，形勢迥殊，攻一碉難於克一城。

translations.literal: Guest and host, labor and ease—the situations differ utterly; taking one diao is harder than taking a city.
translations.idiomatic: Guest fights host on unequal terms; one diao is harder than a city.

sentences.zh: 即臣所駐卡撒，左右山巔三百餘碉，計日以攻，非數年不能盡。

translations.literal: Even at Kasa where I am stationed, there are more than three hundred diao on the left and right peaks; counting days to attack, years would not suffice to take them all.
translations.idiomatic: At Kasa alone more than three hundred diao crown the hills; to take them day by day would take years.

sentences.zh: 且得一碉輒傷數十百人，得不償失。

translations.literal: And for each diao taken dozens or hundreds of men are lost—the gain does not repay the cost.
translations.idiomatic: Each diao costs dozens or hundreds of lives—the gain is not worth the price.

sentences.zh: 兵法，攻堅則瑕者堅，攻瑕則堅者瑕。

translations.literal: In warfare, attack what is strong and the weak become strong; attack what is weak and the strong become weak.
translations.idiomatic: In war, strike the hard point and the soft hardens; strike the soft and the hard weakens.

sentences.zh: 惟使賊失所恃，我兵乃可用其所長。

translations.literal: Only if the enemy is made to lose what they rely on can our troops use their strengths.
translations.idiomatic: Only by depriving the enemy of what they rely on can our troops use their strengths.

sentences.zh: 擬俟諸軍大集，分道而進。

translations.literal: I plan when the armies are fully gathered to advance by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies gather I plan to advance on separate routes.

sentences.zh: 別選銳師，旁探間道，裹糧直入，逾碉勿攻，繞出其後。

translations.literal: Choosing picked troops, scouts will seek by-paths, carry rations and penetrate deep, pass the diao without attacking, and circle behind them.
translations.idiomatic: Picked troops will find by-paths, carry rations, pass the diao without fighting, and strike from behind.

sentences.zh: 番眾不多，外備既密，內守必虛。

translations.literal: The tribesmen are not numerous; with outer defenses thick, inner defense must be thin.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes are few; thick outer defense means thin inner defense.

sentences.zh: 我兵既自捷徑深入，守者各懷內顧，人無固志，均可不攻自潰。

translations.literal: Once our troops penetrate by the swift route, defenders will each look inward, men will lack firm will, and all can collapse without attack.
translations.idiomatic: Once we penetrate by a swift route, defenders will look homeward and collapse without a fight.

sentences.zh: 卡撒為進噶拉依正道，嶺高溝窄，臣當親任其難。

translations.literal: Kasa is the direct road to Gala-i; the ridge is high and the gorge narrow, and I shall personally undertake that hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Kasa is the main road to Gala-i; I shall take that hard road myself.

sentences.zh: 黨壩隘險，亦幾同卡撒，酌益新軍。

translations.literal: Dangba pass is nearly as narrow as Kasa; I shall add fresh troops there as well.
translations.idiomatic: Dangba is almost as narrow as Kasa; I shall reinforce that route too.

sentences.zh: 兩道並進，直搗巢穴，取其渠魁。

translations.literal: Advancing on both routes, we shall strike straight at the nest and seize the chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Both columns will drive at the nest and seize the chiefs.

sentences.zh: 期四月間奏捷。」

translations.literal: I expect to report victory within the fourth month.'
translations.idiomatic: I expect victory by the fourth month.'

sentences.zh: 上以金川非大敵，勞師兩載，誅大臣，失良將，內不懌。

translations.literal: The emperor, holding that Jinchuan was no great enemy yet the army had labored two years, ministers were executed, and good generals lost, was inwardly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Jinchuan no great foe, yet two years of war had cost ministers' lives and good generals, and he was displeased.

sentences.zh: 及是聞其地險難下，益不欲竟其事，遂以孝聖憲皇后諭命班師，而傅恆方督總兵哈攀龍、哈尚德等攻下數碉。

translations.literal: Now hearing the ground was hard to subdue, he was even less willing to press the affair to the end; on the empress dowager's order he recalled the army, while Fu Heng was still directing generals Ha Panlong and Ha Shangde to take several diao.
translations.idiomatic: Learning how hard the country was, he wished to end the war on the empress dowager's order, though Fu Heng was still taking diao under Ha Panlong and Ha Shangde.

sentences.zh: 上以金川水土惡，賜傅恆人蓡三斤，並及諸將有差，屢詔召傅恆還。

translations.literal: Because Jinchuan's climate and water were malignant, the emperor gave Fu Heng three jin of ginseng and varying amounts to the generals, and repeatedly ordered Fu Heng's return.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Fu Heng ginseng and rewards for the generals and repeatedly recalled him, citing Jinchuan's foul climate.

sentences.zh: 又以孝聖憲皇后諭封一等忠勇公，賜寶石頂、四團龍補服。

translations.literal: Again on the empress dowager's order he enfeoffed him duke of the first rank as Duke of Loyal Valor, with a jeweled finial and four-dragon rank patch.
translations.idiomatic: On the empress dowager's order he was made Duke of Loyal Valor of the first rank, with jeweled finial and four-dragon patch.

sentences.zh: 傅恆奏言：「金川事一誤，今復輕率蕆事，賊焰愈張。

translations.literal: Fu Heng memorialized: 'The Jinchuan affair was once mishandled; to end it lightly now will only make the rebels fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng wrote: 'Jinchuan was mishandled once; to end it lightly now will only embolden the rebels.

sentences.zh: 眾土司皆罹其毒，邊宇將無寧日。

translations.literal: All the tribal chiefs suffer their poison; the border will know no peace.
translations.idiomatic: Every tribal chief suffers them; the frontier will never be quiet.

sentences.zh: 審度形勢，賊碉非盡當道，其巢皆老弱，我兵且戰且前，自昔嶺中峰直抵噶拉依，破竹建瓴，功在垂成，棄之可惜。

translations.literal: Judging the situation, not every enemy diao blocks the road; their nests are mostly old and weak; our troops fighting forward from Xiling Peak straight to Gala-i would be like splitting bamboo—success is near and to abandon it would be a pity.
translations.idiomatic: Not every diao blocks the road; their nests are weak; advancing from Xiling Peak to Gala-i would be irresistible, and to stop now would be wasteful.

sentences.zh: 且臣受詔出師，若不掃穴擒渠，何顏返命？」

translations.literal: Moreover, having received orders to take the field, if I do not root out the nest and capture the leaders, with what face can I return to report?'
translations.idiomatic: Having been ordered to campaign, how can I return without destroying the nest and capturing the leaders?'

sentences.zh: 並力辭封賞，上不允，手詔謂：「匈奴未滅，無以家為，乃驃姚武人銳往之概。

translations.literal: He also firmly declined enfeoffment and rewards; the emperor would not allow it and personally wrote: 'Until the Xiongnu are destroyed one cannot make a home—such was the bold spirit of Huo Qubing.
translations.idiomatic: He also refused honors; the emperor refused to accept and wrote: 'Until the Xiongnu are destroyed there is no home—that was Huo Qubing's spirit.

sentences.zh: 大學士抒誠贊化，豈與兜鍪閫帥爭一日之績？」

translations.literal: A grand secretary who expounds sincerity and aids transformation—how should he vie for a single day's merit with helmeted commanders?'
translations.idiomatic: How should a grand secretary who aids the state vie with field commanders for a day's glory?'

sentences.zh: 反复累數千言，复賜詩喻指。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he wrote thousands of words and again bestowed a poem to make his meaning plain.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote thousands of words in personal edicts and sent a poem to make his meaning plain.

sentences.zh: 時傅恆及提督岳鍾琪決策深入，莎羅奔遣頭人乞降，傅恆令自縛詣軍門。

translations.literal: At that time Fu Heng and Commander Yue Zhongqi decided on deep penetration; Slob Dpon sent headmen to beg surrender, and Fu Heng ordered him to bind himself and come to headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng and Yue Zhongqi chose to push deep; Slob Dpon sent headmen to sue for peace, and Fu Heng ordered him bound to camp.

sentences.zh: 莎羅奔复介綽斯甲等詣岳鍾琪乞貸死，鍾琪親入勒烏圍，挈莎羅奔及其子郎卡詣軍門。

translations.literal: Slob Dpon again sent Chuosi Jia and others to Yue Zhongqi to beg for his life; Zhongqi entered Lewuwei in person and brought Slob Dpon and his son Lang Ka to headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Slob Dpon also sent Chuosi Jia to Yue Zhongqi; Zhongqi entered Lewuwei and brought Slob Dpon and his son Lang Ka to camp.

sentences.zh: 語詳鍾琪傳。

translations.literal: The full account is in Zhongqi's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in Yue Zhongqi's biography.

sentences.zh: 傅恆遂受莎羅奔父子降，莎羅奔等焚香作樂，誓六事：無犯鄰比諸番，反其侵地，供役視諸土司，執獻諸酋抗我師者，還所掠內地民馬，納軍械槍砲，乃承製赦其罪。

translations.literal: Fu Heng then accepted the surrender of Slob Dpon and his son; they burned incense and made music, swearing six things: not to harm neighboring tribes, to return invaded lands, to supply labor like other chiefs, to hand over chiefs who had resisted our army, to return people, horses, and goods plundered from the interior, and to surrender weapons, guns, and cannon—then he received the imperial pardon of their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng accepted their surrender on six oaths: no harm to neighbors, return of lands, labor like other chiefs, surrender of resisting chiefs, return of plunder, and delivery of arms—then pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 莎羅奔獻​​佛像一、白金萬，傅恆卻其金，莎羅奔請以金為傅恆建祠。

translations.literal: Slob Dpon presented a Buddha image and ten thousand taels of white silver; Fu Heng refused the silver, and Slob Dpon asked to use the silver to build a shrine to Fu Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Slob Dpon offered a Buddha image and ten thousand taels of silver; Fu Heng refused the silver, and Slob Dpon asked to build him a shrine with it.

sentences.zh: 翌日，傅恆率師還。

translations.literal: The next day Fu Heng led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Fu Heng withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 上優詔嘉獎，命用揚古利故事，賜豹尾槍二桿、親軍二名。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a gracious edict of praise and ordered, following the precedent of Yangguli, the gift of two leopard-tail spears and two guards of the person.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and, following Yangguli's precedent, gave two leopard-tail spears and two personal guards.

sentences.zh: 三月，師至京師，命皇長子及裕親王等郊迎。

translations.literal: In the third month the army reached the capital; the heir apparent and the Prince of Yu and others were ordered to welcome it outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the army reached Beijing; the heir apparent and the Prince of Yu welcomed it outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 上御殿受賀，行飲至禮。

translations.literal: The emperor received congratulations in the hall and held the ritual of drinking to the campaign's end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received congratulations in court and held the victory feast.

sentences.zh: 傅恆疏辭四團龍補服，上命服以入朝，復命用額亦都、佟國維故事，建宗祠，祀曾祖哈什屯以下，並追予李榮保諡，賜第東安門內，以詩落其成。

translations.literal: Fu Heng memorialized to decline the four-dragon patch; the emperor ordered him to wear it at audience and again, following the precedents of Ebilun and Tong Guowei, ordered a ancestral hall built to sacrifice from his great-grandfather Hashitun downward, posthumously enfeoffed Li Rongbao with a title, granted a residence inside the East Gate, and composed a poem on its completion.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng declined the four-dragon patch but was ordered to wear it; a ancestral hall was built after the precedents of Ebilun and Tong Guowei, Li Rongbao was given a posthumous title, and a mansion was granted inside the East Gate.

sentences.zh: 十九年，準噶爾內亂，諸部台吉多內附。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year the Dzungars fell into internal disorder and many taiji of the tribes came over to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: In 1754 the Dzungars fell into civil strife and many tribal taiji submitted.

sentences.zh: 上將用兵，諮廷臣，惟傅恆贊其議。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to use force and consulted the court; only Fu Heng approved the plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned war he consulted the court; only Fu Heng approved.

sentences.zh: 二十年，師克伊犁，俘達瓦齊以歸，諭再封一等公，傅恆固辭，至泣下，乃允之。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the army took Ili and brought Dawachi back captive; the emperor ordered him enfeoffed duke of the first rank again, but Fu Heng firmly declined until he wept, and then it was allowed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1755 Ili was taken and Dawachi captured; the emperor offered him the first-rank dukedom again, but Fu Heng wept and declined until allowed.

sentences.zh: 尋圖功臣像紫光閣，上親制贊，仍以為冠，舉蕭何不戰居首功為比。

translations.literal: Soon portraits of meritorious ministers were painted in the Hall of Purple Splendor; the emperor personally composed encomia and still placed Fu Heng first, comparing him to Xiao He receiving chief merit without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Portraits were painted in the Hall of Purple Splendor; the emperor wrote the praises and still ranked Fu Heng first, comparing him to Xiao He.

sentences.zh: 二十一年四月，將軍策楞追捕阿睦爾撒納未獲，上命傅恆出視師，赴額林哈畢爾噶，集蒙古諸台吉飭軍事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-first year, General Celeng pursued Amursana without catching him; the emperor ordered Fu Heng to oversee the army, go to Irkhabirga, and assemble the Mongol taiji to regulate military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1756 General Celeng failed to catch Amursana; Fu Heng was sent to Irkhabirga to assemble the Mongol taiji.

sentences.zh: 傅恆行日，策楞疏至，已率兵深入，復召傅恆還。

translations.literal: On the day Fu Heng marched, Celeng's memorial arrived saying he had already led troops deep in; Fu Heng was recalled again.
translations.idiomatic: The day Fu Heng set out, Celeng reported he had already advanced deep; Fu Heng was recalled.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，將軍明瑞徵緬甸敗績，二月，授傅恆經略，出督師。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year, after General Mingrui's defeat in the Burma campaign, in the second month Fu Heng was appointed commander-in-chief and went out to supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: In 1768, after Mingrui's defeat in Burma, Fu Heng was made commander-in-chief in the second month.

sentences.zh: 時阿里袞以副將軍主軍事，上並授阿桂副將軍、舒赫德參贊大臣，命舒赫德先赴雲南，與阿里袞籌畫進軍。

translations.literal: At that time Aligun was deputy commander in chief of military affairs; the emperor also appointed Agui deputy commander and Shuhede staff minister, ordering Shuhede to go first to Yunnan to plan the advance with Aligun.
translations.idiomatic: Aligun led as deputy commander; Agui and Shuhede were appointed to assist, and Shuhede went first to Yunnan with Aligun to plan.

sentences.zh: 三十四年二月，傅恆師行，發京師及滿、蒙兵一萬三千六百人從征，上御太和殿賜敕，賚御用甲胄。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirty-fourth year Fu Heng's army marched; thirteen thousand six hundred Manchu and Mongol troops from the capital followed the campaign; the emperor in the Hall of Supreme Harmony bestowed his command and imperial armor.
translations.idiomatic: In February 1769 Fu Heng marched with 13,600 Manchu and Mongol troops; the emperor bestowed command and armor in the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 四月，至騰越，傅恆決策，師循戛鳩江而進，大兵出江西，取道猛拱、猛養，直搗木梳，水師沿江順流下，水陸相應。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he reached Tengyue; Fu Heng decided the army should advance along the Jiugu River; the main force would leave west of the river, take the Menggong and Mengyang route, and strike straight at Mushu, while the navy descended with the current—land and water cooperating.
translations.idiomatic: At Tengyue he decided to advance along the Jiugu: the main column west through Menggong and Mengyang toward Mushu, the fleet downstream in concert.

sentences.zh: 偏師出江東取猛密，夾擊老官屯。

translations.literal: A detached column would leave east of the river to take Mengmi and strike Laoguantun from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: A flank column east of the river would take Mengmi and pinch Laoguantun.

sentences.zh: 往歲以避瘴，九月後進兵，緬甸得為備。

translations.literal: In past years, to avoid miasma, troops advanced only after the ninth month, giving Burma time to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly troops waited until after the ninth month to avoid miasma, letting Burma prepare.

sentences.zh: 傅恆互議先數十日出不意，攻其未備，水師當具舟。

translations.literal: Fu Heng urged advancing several tens of days early by surprise before they were ready; the navy must have boats.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng urged advancing weeks early by surprise; the fleet must have boats.

sentences.zh: 上初命阿里袞造舟濟師，阿里袞等言崖險澗窄不宜舟，傍江亦無造舟所。

translations.literal: The emperor had first ordered Aligun to build boats to ferry the army; Aligun and others said cliffs were steep, streams narrow, boats unsuitable, and there was no place to build them along the river.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had ordered boats built; Aligun said the cliffs and streams forbade it and there was no shipyard.

sentences.zh: 上又命三泰、傅顯往視，言與阿里袞等同。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered Santai and Fuxian to inspect; they reported the same as Aligun.
translations.idiomatic: Santai and Fuxian were sent to inspect and agreed with Aligun.

sentences.zh: 及傅恆至軍，諮土司頭人，知蠻暮有山曰翁古多木，旁有地曰野牛壩，野人所居，涼爽無瘴。

translations.literal: When Fu Heng reached the army he consulted tribal headmen and learned that at Manmu was a mountain called Wengguduomu and beside it a place called Yeniuba where wild tribes lived—cool and without miasma.
translations.idiomatic: At the front Fu Heng learned from headmen of Wengguduomu near Manmu and the cool, miasma-free Yeniuba.

sentences.zh: 即地伐木造舟，野人樂受值，執役甚謹。

translations.literal: There they felled timber and built boats; the tribesmen gladly took pay and worked very diligently.
translations.idiomatic: There they cut timber for boats; tribesmen gladly worked for pay.

sentences.zh: 傅恆即使傅顯佐蒞事。

translations.literal: Fu Heng had Fuxian assist in supervising the work.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng put Fuxian in charge.

sentences.zh: 舟成，督滿、漢兵並從行奴僕，更番轉搬。

translations.literal: When the boats were finished, Manchu and Han troops and their servants were organized in relays to portage them.
translations.idiomatic: When the boats were done, troops and servants relayed them in turns.

sentences.zh: 又得茂隆廠附近砲工，令範銅為砲。

translations.literal: Gunsmiths were also obtained near the Maolong works to cast bronze cannon.
translations.idiomatic: Gunsmiths from Maolong were set to cast bronze guns.

sentences.zh: 狀聞，輒降旨嘉獎，為賦造舟行焉。

translations.literal: When reports arrived, the emperor repeatedly issued edicts of praise and composed a poem on building the boats.
translations.idiomatic: Each report brought imperial praise and a poem on boat-building.

sentences.zh: 傅恆初議自將九千三百人渡戛鳩而西，師未集，七月，將四千人發騰越。

translations.literal: Fu Heng had first planned to lead nine thousand three hundred men across the Jiugu westward; the army was not yet gathered, and in the seventh month he sent four thousand from Tengyue.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng first planned to lead 9,300 men across the Jiugu; in July, before the army gathered, he sent 4,000 from Tengyue.

sentences.zh: 上以經略自將師寡，促諸軍速集如初議。

translations.literal: The emperor, holding that the commander-in-chief leading in person with too few troops, urged the armies to gather quickly as first planned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought the commander-in-chief had too few men and urged the armies to gather as planned.

sentences.zh: 八月，傅恆自南蚌趨戛鳩。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Fu Heng hurried from Nanbang toward the Jiugu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Fu Heng rushed from Nanbang to the Jiugu.

sentences.zh: 奏至，上方行圍木蘭，入圍獲狍，畀福隆安以賜傅恆。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived the emperor was hunting at Mulan; entering the hunt he took a roe deer and had Fulong'an present it to Fu Heng as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived the emperor was at the Mulan hunt and sent a roe deer by Fulong'an as gift to Fu Heng.

sentences.zh: 傅恆道南底壩至允帽，臨戛鳩江，時猛拱大頭人脫猛烏猛、頭人賀丙等，詣傅恆請降。

translations.literal: Fu Heng went from Nandiba to Yunmao on the Jiugu; at that time the great headman of Menggong, Tuomengwumeng, and headman He Bing and others came to Fu Heng to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jiugu, Tuomengwumeng of Menggong and He Bing came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 師至，脫猛烏猛將夾江諸夷寨頭人來迎，與賀丙具舟。

translations.literal: When the army arrived, Tuomengwumeng brought headmen of tribal stockades along both banks to welcome it, and with He Bing provided boats.
translations.idiomatic: Tuomengwumeng brought riverside headmen to welcome the army, and he and He Bing supplied boats.

sentences.zh: 傅恆命分兵徐濟，夾江為寨猛拱后土司渾覺亦請降，獻馴象四。

translations.literal: Fu Heng ordered troops ferried in detachments; stockades were set along the river; the Menggong queen-regent Hunjue also surrendered and presented four tame elephants.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng ferried troops in detachments and set riverside camps; Queen Hunjue of Menggong surrendered with four elephants.

sentences.zh: 上賚三眼孔雀翎，傅恆疏辭。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed a three-eyed peacock feather; Fu Heng memorialized to decline.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave a three-eyed peacock feather; Fu Heng declined.

sentences.zh: 師復進，取猛養，破寨四，誅頭人拉匿拉賽。

translations.literal: The army advanced again, took Mengyang, broke four stockades, and executed headman Lanilasai.
translations.idiomatic: The army took Mengyang, stormed four stockades, and executed headman Lanilasai.

sentences.zh: 設台站，令瑚爾起以七百人駐守。

translations.literal: Relay stations were established and Hu Erqi was left with seven hundred men to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Relay stations were set up and Hu Erqi garrisoned with 700 men.

sentences.zh: 遂至南董幹，攻南準寨，獲頭人木波猛等三十五人。

translations.literal: Then they reached Nandonggan, attacked the Nanzhun stockade, and captured thirty-five headmen including Mubomeng.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Nandonggan, took the Nanzhun stockade, and captured thirty-five headmen including Mubomeng.

sentences.zh: 進次暮臘，再進次新街。

translations.literal: Advancing they halted at Mula, then advanced again to Xinjie.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced to Mula, then pushed on to Xinjie.

sentences.zh: 傅恆自渡戛鳩江，未嘗與緬甸兵戰，刈禾為糧，行二千里不血刃，而士馬觸暑雨多疾病。

translations.literal: From the time Fu Heng crossed the Jiugu he had not fought Burmese troops; reaping grain for provisions, he marched two thousand li without drawing a blade, yet men and horses suffered many illnesses from heat and rain.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the Jiugu Fu Heng fought no Burmese troops; he lived off the harvest and marched two thousand li unblooded, but heat and rain brought widespread sickness.

sentences.zh: 會阿桂將萬餘人自虎踞關出野牛壩，造舟畢成，徵廣東、福建水師亦至，乃合軍並進。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Agui led more than ten thousand men out from Huju Pass to Yeniuba; when boat-building was finished and the Guangdong and Fujian naval forces also arrived, the armies united and advanced together.
translations.idiomatic: Agui brought more than ten thousand men from Huju Pass to Yeniuba; when the boats were ready and Guangdong and Fujian fleets arrived, the armies joined and advanced.

sentences.zh: 哈國興將水師，阿桂、阿里袞將陸師，阿桂出江東，阿里袞出江西。

translations.literal: Ha Guoxing commanded the navy; Agui and Aligun commanded the land forces; Agui went out east of the river and Aligun west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Ha Guoxing led the fleet; Agui and Aligun the land forces—Agui east of the river, Aligun west.

sentences.zh: 緬兵壘金沙江兩岸，又以舟師扼江口。

translations.literal: Burmese troops fortified both banks of the Jinsha and also used a fleet to hold the river mouth.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese fortified both banks of the Jinsha and blocked the mouth with boats.

sentences.zh: 阿桂先與緬兵遇，麾步兵發銃矢，又以騎兵陷陣，緬兵潰。

translations.literal: Agui first met Burmese troops, ordered the infantry to fire muskets and arrows, and also sent cavalry to break the formation; the Burmese routed.
translations.idiomatic: Agui met the Burmese first, poured musket and arrow fire into them, sent cavalry to break their line, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 哈國興督舟師乘風蹴敵，緬兵舟相擊，死者數千。

translations.literal: Ha Guoxing directed the fleet to strike the enemy with the wind; Burmese boats collided and several thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Ha Guoxing drove the fleet downwind into the enemy; thousands died as boats collided.

sentences.zh: 阿里袞亦破西岸緬兵，傅恆以所獲纛進。

translations.literal: Aligun also broke the Burmese on the west bank; Fu Heng presented the captured banners.
translations.idiomatic: Aligun broke the west-bank Burmese as well, and Fu Heng sent up the captured banners.

sentences.zh: 上復為賦詩，阿里袞感瘴而病，改將水師，旋卒。

translations.literal: The emperor again composed a poem; Aligun fell ill from miasma, was changed to command the navy, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote another poem; Aligun took miasma fever, switched to the fleet, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 十一月，傅恆復進攻老官屯，老官屯在金沙江東，東猛密，西猛墅，北猛拱、猛養，南緬都阿瓦，為水陸通衢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Fu Heng again advanced on Laoguantun; Laoguantun lies east of the Jinsha, with Mengmi to the east and Mengshu to the west, Menggong and Mengyang to the north and the Burmese capital Ava to the south—a thoroughfare for land and water.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Fu Heng attacked Laoguantun on the Jinsha, the junction of Mengmi, Mengshu, Menggong, Mengyang, and the road to Ava.

sentences.zh: 緬兵伐木立寨甚固，哈國興督諸軍力攻，未即克。

translations.literal: Burmese troops felled timber and built a very solid stockade; Ha Guoxing directed all armies in a fierce assault but did not take it at once.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese built a timber stockade; Ha Guoxing assaulted it hard but could not take it quickly.

sentences.zh: 師破東南木寨，緬兵夜自水寨出，傅恆令海蘭察御之，又令伊勒圖督舟師掩擊，复獲船纛。

translations.literal: The army broke the southeastern timber stockade; Burmese troops came out at night from the water stockade; Fu Heng ordered Hailancha to repel them and Yiletui to direct the fleet in a surprise attack, again capturing boats and banners.
translations.idiomatic: Our troops took the southeast timber camp; the Burmese sallied by night from the water camp; Hailancha repelled them and Yiletui's fleet seized more boats and banners.

sentences.zh: 緬兵潛至江岸築壘，又自林箐中出，海蘭察擊之，屢有斬馘。

translations.literal: Burmese troops secretly came to the riverbank to build forts and also emerged from the forest thickets; Hailancha struck them and repeatedly took heads.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese built riverside forts and struck from the woods; Hailancha beat them back again and again.

sentences.zh: 師久攻堅，士卒染瘴多物故，水陸軍三萬一千，至是僅存一萬三千。

translations.literal: The army had long assaulted strong positions; soldiers contracted miasma and many died; of thirty-one thousand land and water troops, only thirteen thousand now remained.
translations.idiomatic: After long assaults, miasma killed many; of 31,000 land and water troops only 13,000 remained.

sentences.zh: 傅恆以入告，上命罷兵，召傅恆還京。

translations.literal: Fu Heng reported this; the emperor ordered the campaign ended and Fu Heng recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng reported the losses; the emperor ended the campaign and recalled him.

sentences.zh: 傅恆俄亦病，阿桂以聞。

translations.literal: Fu Heng soon fell ill himself; Agui reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng soon fell ill; Agui informed the court.

sentences.zh: 上令即馳驛還，而以軍事付阿桂。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to return post-haste by courier relay and entrusted military affairs to Agui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered him home by relay post and left the army to Agui.

sentences.zh: 會緬甸酋懵駁遣頭人諾爾塔齎蒲葉書乞罷兵，傅恆奏入，上許其行成。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Burmese chief Meng Bo sent headman Nuoerta with a palm-leaf letter begging to cease hostilities; Fu Heng memorialized it and the emperor permitted a settlement.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese chief Meng Bo sent Nuoerta with a palm-leaf plea for peace; Fu Heng reported it and the emperor agreed to truce.

sentences.zh: 傅恆附疏言：「用兵之始，眾以為難。

translations.literal: Fu Heng appended a memorial saying: 'At the start of the campaign all held it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng added: 'When war began everyone called it hard.

sentences.zh: 臣執意請行，負委任，請從重治罪。」

translations.literal: I insisted on going and have failed my commission; I ask to be punished severely.'
translations.idiomatic: I insisted on going and failed my charge; punish me severely.'

sentences.zh: 上手詔謂：「用兵非得已，如以為非是，朕當首任其過。

translations.literal: The emperor's personal edict said: 'Using force is never willingly chosen; if you think it wrong, I should bear the blame first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote: 'War is never chosen lightly; if it was wrong, I should bear the blame.

sentences.zh: 皇祖時，吳三桂請撤籓，諮於群臣，議撤者惟米思翰、明珠數人。

translations.literal: In our grandfather's time, when Wu Sangui asked to withdraw the fief, the emperor consulted the ministers; only Misanhan, Mingzhu, and a few others favored withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Kangxi Emperor, when Wu Sangui asked to give up his fief, only Misanhan, Mingzhu, and a few others favored withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 及三桂反，眾請誅議撤諸臣，皇祖深闢其非。

translations.literal: When Sangui rebelled, many asked that the ministers who had favored withdrawal be executed; the grandfather deeply rejected that as wrong.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangui rebelled, many wanted those ministers killed; the grandfather firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 朕仰紹祖訓，傅恆此事，可援以相比。

translations.literal: I follow our grandfather's teaching; Fu Heng's case may be compared to this.
translations.idiomatic: I follow that teaching; Fu Heng's case is like it.

sentences.zh: 傅恆收猛拱，當賜三眼孔雀翎，疏辭，俟功成拜賜。

translations.literal: Fu Heng recovered Menggong and should receive the three-eyed peacock feather; he memorialized to decline, asking to receive it only when merit was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: For recovering Menggong he should have the three-eyed peacock feather; he declined until victory.

sentences.zh: 今既未克賊巢，當繳進賜翎，以稱其請罪之意。」

translations.literal: Now that the enemy nest has not been taken, he should return the gifted feather to match his plea for punishment.'
translations.idiomatic: Since the nest was not taken, he should return the feather to match his plea for guilt.'

sentences.zh: 懵駁遣頭人詣軍獻方物。

translations.literal: Meng Bo sent headmen to the army presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Bo sent headmen with tribute to the army.

sentences.zh: 十月，傅恆還駐虎踞關，上命傅恆會雲貴總督彰寶議減雲南總兵、知府員缺，釐正州縣舊制。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Fu Heng returned to garrison at Huju Pass; the emperor ordered Fu Heng to meet with Yunnan-Guizhou Governor Zhang Bao to discuss reducing the posts of Yunnan regional commander and prefect, and rectifying the old system of prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Fu Heng garrisoned Huju Pass and met Governor Zhang Bao to reform Yunnan's military and civil posts.

sentences.zh: 三十四年二月，班師。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirty-fourth year the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1769 the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三月，上幸天津，傅恆朝行在。

translations.literal: In the third month the emperor visited Tianjin; Fu Heng attended audience at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the emperor went to Tianjin and Fu Heng attended him on the journey.

sentences.zh: 既而緬甸酋謝罪表久不至，上謂傅恆方病，不忍治其罪。

translations.literal: Later the Burmese chief's letter of apology long failed to arrive; the emperor said Fu Heng was ill and could not bear to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: When Burma's apology lagged, the emperor spared Fu Heng because he was ill.

sentences.zh: 七月，卒，上親臨其第酹酒，命喪葬視宗室鎮國公，諡文忠。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he died; the emperor personally visited his house to pour libation, ordered funeral rites equal to a clansman prince of the blood of the third degree, and gave the posthumous title Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he died; the emperor poured libation at his house, gave him a prince's funeral, and posthumous title Wenzong.

sentences.zh: 又命入祀前所建宗祠。

translations.literal: He was also ordered enshrined in the ancestral hall built earlier.
translations.idiomatic: He was also enshrined in the hall built for his family.

sentences.zh: 其後上复幸天津，念傅恆於此復命，又經傅恆墓賜奠，皆紀以詩。

translations.literal: Later when the emperor again visited Tianjin, remembering Fu Heng's audience there, and passing Fu Heng's tomb bestowed sacrifice—all were recorded in poems.
translations.idiomatic: Later visits to Tianjin and offerings at Fu Heng's tomb were all remembered in the emperor's poems.

sentences.zh: 及賦懷舊詩，許為「社稷臣」。

translations.literal: In his poem recalling old ministers he allowed him to be called a 'pillar of the state.'
translations.idiomatic: In a poem of remembrance he called Fu Heng a 'pillar of the state.'

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，以福康安平苗功，贈貝子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, because Fukang'an pacified the Miao, Fu Heng was posthumously given the rank of beile.
